newsitem.title: NEPAL: Nepal eyes Tibetan market through joint ventures.
newsitem.headline: Nepal eyes Tibetan market through joint ventures.

text.p: Businessmen from Nepal have asked China to set up joint ventures in the Himalayan kingdom to tap the Tibetan market, saying exporting goods from Nepal would be easier than transporting them from mainland China.
Nepali businessmen made the suggestion at a trade promotion meeting with their Chinese counterparts on Thursday, officials said.

Padma Jyoti, president of the Federation of Nepalese Chambers and Industry (FNCCI), said Nepal could be "ideal" for meeting the demands for products across the Himalayas in Tibet, which is undergoing "major reconstruction and development".
A trans-Himalayan highway built by the Chinese government in the 1960s links Kathmandu with the Tibetan capital, Lhasa.

An agreement to boost bilateral trade was concluded at a meeting of the Nepal-China Non-governmental Cooperation Forum that ended on Thursday. A trade and investment seminar was also held to identify potential areas for joint ventures.

FNCCI vice-president Pradeep Kumar Shrestha, who led the Nepali team at the talks, told reporters the two sides signed an agreement to explore hydro-power, pharmaceuticals, cement and poultry farming joint ventures in Nepal.
Nepali exports to China totalled $4.7 million and imports were $57.6 million in fiscal 1994-95. The Nepali fiscal year begins in mid-July.
